BiblicalUsage: libbâh means the heart — an ordinary word that carries real weight in the Bible. In Proverbs 17:3, "and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts."; and in Psalms 7:9, "but establish the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.". In Proverbs 21:2, "Every way of a man [is] right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts."; and in Ezekiel 16:30, "How weak is thine heart".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heart is the furnace God tests — the fining pot is for silver, but the Lord trieth the hearts. I hold that every way of a man is right in his own eyes, yet the Lord pondereth the hearts and is not fooled. My position is that a weak heart, honestly given to God, is stronger than a proud one He must break.
